messages.subject: Work group tomorrow (6 Oct)
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

Just a friendly reminder the the R users’ group will be meeting tomorrow from 10-noon in the Data Lab classroom (360 Shields Library) and online. Join us with your trickiest R questions, or just come hang out and use the space for dedicated coding practice. If you join remotely, please post your questions to the discord site ahead of time. Relevant links below.

Best,
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

_______________________________________

The fall quaRter is upon us, which means we have a whole academic term of Davis R Users' Group (D-RUG) to look forward to. This quarter, D-RUG will be meeting from 10am-noon on Wednesdays. We will be meeting in a hybrid format, in 360 Shields Library (DataLab classroom) and on Zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>. You are cordially invited to attend in either venue.

This year, we are adopting a new queueing approach for virtual folks seeking help at D-RUG. If you are joining virtually, we ask that you submit your question to our Discourse site <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> in advance of our meetings, and we will address folks' questions in the order they are received. Of course, you are always welcome (and encouraged) to just come hang out, and use the work group time as a dedicated chunk of time to get some coding done with good company.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar <https://d-rug.github.io/calendar.html>! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).
--
Christian John — Ph.D. candidate

messages.subject: Next week: Contrasts, factors, and the emmeans package
messages.subject_clean: Next week: Contrasts, factors, and the emmeans package
messages.body_plain:
Hi fRiends,

The Davis R Users Group will hold its regularly scheduled weekly meeting 10am-12pm next Wednesday, October 13. The meeting will begin with a short presentation on the topics of factor coding, contrasts, and examining model fits with the emmeans package. The goal is to explain how R handles factor variables, and how to interpret models that use factors. The meeting will be hybrid-virtual, with attendance in-person at room 360 Shields Library or virtually over Zoom. Our presenter is Wesley Brooks, statistician at the UC Davis DataLab. Following the presentation, there will be free time to co-work and/or ask questions of other R Users.

Best wishes,
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.body_plain:
Reminder that this workshop is tomorrow!  Sign up ahead of time so you’ve got the zoom link when it starts.

Michele

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Specialist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

Data & Digital Scholarship

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

From: geospatia...@ucdavis.edu <geospatia...@ucdavis.edu> On Behalf Of Matthew Conner
Sent: Tuesday, October 12, 2021 10:46 PM
To: geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [geospatial] #maptimeDavis Workshop: Interactive Maps in R Shiny

#MAPTIMEDAVIS: INTERACTIVE MAPS IN R SHINY
OCTOBER 19 @ 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM

Description

Learn how to create and customize professional-quality, interactive maps in R shiny. Allow users to explore data, provide both spatial and non-spatial inputs, and receive personalized feedback.

Learning Objectives

o Create a local R shiny app with an interactive map
o Add customized data to an interactive map
o Collect user input (spatial and non-spatial)
o Give feedback to user based on combined data and user inputs.

Prerequisites

o Introductory knowledge of R
o Introductory knowledge of spatial data

Software

R (version 4.1.0 or newer) and R Studio. Download R at https://cran.r-project.org/ and R Studio at https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/

Instructor: Taylor Nelsen

Instructor Bio

Taylor Nelsen is an Assistant Specialist in the Grain Cropping Systems lab in the Department of Plant Sciences at UC Davis. Her research and extension efforts focus on nitrogen management, plant phenotyping, and variety selection using traditional agronomic methods in conjunction with new technologies such as drones, satellites, and web-based decision support tools.

Location: Zoom. Please register to receive Zoom link.

Registration: https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/maptimeDavisInteractiveMapsRshiny/register/

Cost: Free of charge.

More Upcoming #maptimeDavis Events:

October 26, 2021  I <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-getting-started-with-arcgis-online/>ntro to ArcGIS Online <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-getting-started-with-arcgis-online/> - Karen Beardsley

November 2, 2021  ArcGIS Field Maps (ESRI) <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-arcgis-field-maps/> - Miriam Schmidts and Canserina Kurnia

November 9, 2021  Intro to PostGIS with Crunchy Data <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-introduction-to-postgis-with-crunchy-data/> - Steve Pousty

November 16, 2021  I <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-introduction-to-desktop-gis-with-qgis/>ntro to Desktop GIS with QGIS <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/maptimedavis-introduction-to-desktop-gis-with-qgis/> - Michele Tobias

*** The full schedule with links to each event is on the Spatial Sciences Research & Learning Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> page. ***

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the DataLab YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTooXK1RiSHNbWsmeqz0W6g>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu

Matt Conner

Student Services Department

Library

University of California, Davis

on behalf of the #maptimeDavis council

messages.subject: Internal postdoc opportunities in biomedical data science training at UC Davis
messages.subject_clean: Internal postdoc opportunities in biomedical data science training at UC Davis
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

We seek _current_ postdocs (or graduating PhD students) at UC Davis to join a small team of staff and researchers to do training and engagement as part of the [NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE)](http://nih-cfde.org/).

This opportunity may be of particular interest to postdocs who are seeking industry positions in biotech and would like hands-on experience and training in online training, asynchronous projects, GitHub-based material development, workflow execution, and cloud computing.

Unfortunately this opportunity is limited to those who are already employed at UC Davis but whose funding is expiring. Applicants must be eligible for an extension to their postdoc position; we can also potentially hire newly graduated PhDs and PhD students on filing fee. Please contact us if you are interested.

For more details and contact information, please see the below page.

https://hackmd.io/@ctb/HkQouAO7F

thank you,
—titus
---

Dr. C. Titus Brown, ctb...@ucdavis.edu
Professor, UC Davis
http://ivory.idyll.org/lab/
